key_insight: Interfacial suboxide bonding couples tensile deformation to localized bond weakening and crystallographic facet-dependent electronic responses in oxidized silicon nanowires.
engineering_relevance: Controlling interface chemistry and facet orientation could help tune strain-sensitive nanoelectronics while limiting localized mechanical failure.
method: Simulate dry thermal oxidation using reactive force field molecular dynamics.
Track interfacial bond evolution and stress gradients under tensile strain.
Use density functional theory on facet-specific models to assess electronic responses.
evidence_signal: Simulations show elongated, lower-bond-order interfacial Si–Si bonds with preferential rupture, while first-principles calculations reveal facet-dependent electronic responses to strain.
watch_item: The abstract reports computational findings without experimental validation or quantitative device-performance benchmarks.
paper_title: Strain-Induced Interfacial Bond Evolution and Facet-dependent Strain Response of Electronic Properties in Oxidized Silicon Nanowires
